scope: Post-review robustness analyses; this is repository provenance, not external preregistration.

amendments.timing: Scale Seen candidates had been executed, but no scale portfolio analysis or Unseen candidate evaluation had completed; every downstream experiment was still waiting.
amendments.rationale: The frozen protocol and manuscript bind every policy to the cached current-program baseline, but four new Python runners repeated that execution. Load-sensitive timeout outcomes then made identical baselines disagree. The fix reuses the pre-existing split cache and recomputes only baseline-dependent fields and summaries.
amendments.impact: Training, generated programs, generated-program execution outcomes, TED values, split membership, selectors, and analysis code are unchanged. Validation and test baseline pass rates, improvement labels, and fallback composition are deterministically rebound before selection or final analysis.

amendments.timing: The exercise-heldout CodeWorkout analysis had completed. Prompt-distribution control exited while materializing its first current-only dataset, before any prompt-control candidate generation or evaluation; problem cross-fitting and verdict-order retraining were still waiting on completion markers.
amendments.rationale: Under Bash set -u, the prompt runner assigned a local name and expanded that name for another local initializer in the same command. Bash expands all initializers before completing the assignments, so the runner exited with an unbound-variable error. The same latent declaration pattern in the still-waiting verdict-order runner was corrected before it executed.
amendments.impact: Only local declarations were split into sequential statements. Dataset definitions, checkpoints, prompts, decoding, generation budget, execution, selectors, endpoints, and analysis code are unchanged. Prompt control restarted from zero completed candidates; no partial generation or evaluation was reused.

amendments.timing: The first problem-cross-fit attempt stopped during its pre-analysis baseline-consistency check; no cross-fit result file had been produced. The scale, CodeWorkout, and prompt-distribution experiments had completed, while verdict-order retraining was independent of this runner.
amendments.rationale: The cross-fit runner reused previously generated mixed and Answer validation/test caches. Although downstream generated candidates were normalized, the reused caches themselves still contained load-sensitive current-program baseline executions, so the frozen equality check rejected them. The fix applies the already declared deterministic cached-baseline normalization to both reused families before selection and analysis.
amendments.impact: No training, generated program, generated-program execution outcome, TED value, split, fold, selector, endpoint, or analysis formula changed. Only current-program baseline-dependent fields in the reused mixed and Answer caches are rebound to the canonical split cache before the previously failing consistency check.

amendments.timing: The batch-one pilot had generated 45 of 997 Seen candidates for its first sampling seed. It was stopped before any candidate execution, composed controller output, statistical analysis, or result inspection.
amendments.rationale: Batch-one sampling used only about 59 percent GPU utilization. The replacement evaluates a fixed seed pass in batches of four and forbids resume for batched sampling, so interruption regenerates the entire pass from the same global seed rather than changing batch membership or RNG state.
amendments.impact: The fixed Answer2027 checkpoint, three sampling seeds, temperature, top-p, prompt, datasets, candidate budget, execution limits, composition, endpoints, and analysis are unchanged. The incomplete pilot file is overwritten; batching changes the realized pseudorandom draws but was fixed before any execution outcome was observed.

amendments.timing: The synchronous batch runner had generated 264 of 997 Seen candidates for its first seed. It was stopped before any candidate execution, composed controller output, statistical analysis, or generated-text inspection.
amendments.rationale: Synchronous generation forced short completions to wait for the longest completion in each batch. The installed vLLM engine supports the same local 4-bit base model, LoRA adapter, per-example deterministic seeds, and sampling parameters while continuously scheduling requests of different lengths.
amendments.impact: Checkpoint, prompt rendering, three seed identities, temperature, top-p, token/context limits, datasets, candidate budget, execution, composition, endpoints, and analysis are unchanged. The incomplete generation file is overwritten. The engine can realize different pseudorandom samples under the same seeds, but the change was fixed before any program execution or outcome inspection.

amendments.timing: The first same-draw decomposition attempt terminated while vLLM was rendering requests, before producing any generation file, candidate execution, composed portfolio, statistical analysis, or result inspection.
amendments.rationale: vLLM 0.18 allocated 92 percent of device memory to model and KV cache, leaving insufficient temporary memory for a bitsandbytes matrix multiplication. Reducing the requested cache fraction to 82 percent preserves several GiB of operator workspace.
amendments.impact: Checkpoint, prompts, datasets, three seed identities, sampling parameters, token limits, candidate budget, execution, composition, endpoints, and analysis are unchanged. No candidate from the failed attempt exists or is reused.

stochastic_one_decomposition.design: Generate three newly fixed Answer2027 samples with seeds 4101, 4102, and 4103 at temperature 0.8 and top-p 0.95. Evaluate each sample as a one-candidate policy and evaluate the execution-selected union of those identical three draws. The primary breadth estimand is union RR minus the mean one-draw RR, with problem-cluster bootstrap intervals. Greedy Answer2027 is retained only to estimate the decoding-mode contrast. Seen and Unseen test outcomes are not used to choose seeds, candidates, or analysis.

seen_hidden_and_training_overlap.design: Partition every Seen problem testcase by SHA-256 with seed 52027, expose only the observed half in prompts and selection, and require selected patches to pass both observed and untouched hidden halves. Evaluate the already validation-frozen unrestricted mixed portfolio (Answer2028, Progress2027, Strict2028) and Answer-9Choose3 control (Answer2032, Answer2033, Answer2034). Separately compare each selected returned program with every same-problem Answer training target using exact normalized AST and maximum lexical-token similarity. Report overlap separately for repaired and unrepaired generated selections; overlap is treated as compatible with, but not proof of, memorization.
